summary.text: In April 1815, Mount Tambora on the island of Sumbawa, in today's Indonesia, produced the most powerful volcanic eruption in recorded human history.
Rated 7 on the volcanic explosivity index, it threw 37–45 km³ of dense-rock-equivalent material into the atmosphere.
Its ash spread around the world and lowered global temperatures, bringing the 1816 Year Without a Summer, with extreme weather and failed harvests.

facts.label: Height lost
facts.value: Peak fell from about 4,300 m to 2,851 m

facts.label: Eruption column
facts.value: Reached over 43 km, into the stratosphere

items.prompt: Why did 1816 become known in many places as the Year Without a Summer?

options.label: A long solar eclipse darkened the sky
Tambora's ash cooled the whole world
Wars burned forests and blocked sunlight
A comet passed close and chilled the air

items.explain: Ash from Tambora's eruption column spread around the world and lowered global temperatures, causing extreme weather and harvest failures.

items.prompt: Fine ash from Tambora drifted high around the globe for months. What did people in London see in 1815?

options.label: Long, brilliantly coloured sunsets
Grey ash falling like snow in streets
Several days of total darkness
Constant rumbling like distant thunder

items.explain: Winds spread the fine particles worldwide, creating optical effects such as prolonged, brilliantly coloured sunsets seen in London.

items.prompt: What happened to Mount Tambora's height because of the 1815 explosion?

options.label: It grew taller from new lava
It stayed almost exactly the same
It dropped by about a third
It sank below sea level

items.explain: The peak was about 4,300 m before the explosion and only 2,851 m after, a loss of about one-third.

items.prompt: Tambora sat quiet for centuries before 1815. What was happening deep underground during that time?

options.label: Its magma chamber was slowly draining away
The volcano had become fully extinct
Seawater was steadily cooling the rock
Magma cooled in a closed chamber, building pressure

items.explain: As water-rich magma cooled and crystallised in its closed chamber, high-pressure fluid formed and over-pressurised the chamber.

items.prompt: After the eruption, uprooted trees mixed with pumice washed into the sea. What did they form?

options.label: A new island joined to the shore
Floating rafts up to 5 km across
A reef that blocked the harbour
Nothing, as they sank at once

items.explain: Uprooted trees mixed with pumice ash formed rafts up to 5 km across, and ships later met pumice rafts about 3,600 km west of Tambora.

items.prompt: On 10 April, people in Trumon, Sumatra, more than 2,600 km away, heard Tambora. What did they first think the sound was?

options.label: Thunder from an approaching storm
Waves pounding on the coast
Guns being fired
A nearby landslide

items.explain: The distant booms were first taken for the sound of firing guns.
